fatal_errors: The proposed electrochemical dealloying route is not the reported spray-drying/thermal decomposition-reduction method.
The initial state is incorrectly specified as an as-cast HEA ingot rather than spray-dried, compositionally homogeneous mixed-salt precursor particles.
The proposed electrolyte, potential, temperature, dealloying time, ligament size, and porosity are unsupported by any cited evidence.
The selective-dissolution mechanism contradicts the target hydrogen-assisted sequential reduction and incorporation mechanism.
The hypothesis omits the key role of Pt, Ir, or Ru in enabling single-phase alloy formation and the failure of Pd and noble-metal-free controls.
It does not address the experimentally demonstrated fcc/hcp phase selection and thermally activated Pt-Ru phase transformation.
explanation: The response recognizes the broad objective of making an NM-HEA three-dimensional porous framework, and its proposed microscopy/porosity experiment could test whether dealloying produces such a morphology. However, it reconstructs none of the central synthesis, conditions, formation mechanism, controls, phase behavior, or catalytic outcomes of the target work. The target method is spray drying of mixed aqueous salts followed by H2 reduction, normally at 300°C for 30 minutes. Framework formation proceeds through early reduction of Pt, Ir, or Ru, hydrogen dissociation on the newborn noble-metal surface, and subsequent reduction and lattice incorporation of transition metals. Because the dealloying proposal and its quantitative parameters have no supporting evidence, it is an unsupported alternative rather than a supported reconstruction.
